{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABYY1jWA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhB8xYY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 15, "title": "Pivot to a reproducible Qwen2.5-0.5B LoRA JSON-extraction benchmark", "body": "## Problem

Our current Qwen3-4B / MBPP code-generation experiments have not shown a reproducible benefit from LoRA, even after fixing padding-loss masking and testing multiple learning rates and training seeds. We first need a **positive-control fine-tuning experiment**: a small, practical task with publicly documented before/after improvement. This will help establish that our Apple Silicon training and evaluation workflow can demonstrably change performance under a known recipe before revisiting harder coding tasks.

The reference project [openatlaspro-AI/mlx-lora-finetune](https://github.com/openatlaspro-AI/mlx-lora-finetune) reports freight/shipment text → structured JSON extraction with **mlx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit**. Its committed [comparison](https://github.com/openatlaspro-AI/mlx-lora-finetune/blob/main/results/comparison.md) reports **71.3% (base) → 100.0% (LoRA)** overall exact-record accuracy on 150 held-out synthetic examples, after a 600-step, batch-4, rank-8 LoRA training run. These are **the upstream author's results, not yet our independent reproduction**; improvement must be measured anew.

## Expected outcome

Repurpose `takahirox/llm-finetuning` into a **minimal, reproducible local positive-control LoRA demo** on Apple Silicon:

1. Reproduce the reference experiment as faithfully as feasible, including synthetic data generation, prompt/schema normalization, original 4-bit model, LoRA recipe, and held-out scoring.
2. Run both the base and a **freshly trained** local adapter on the same held-out examples, reporting actual JSON validity, all-fields-exact accuracy, and per-field accuracy, plus the absolute before/after difference.
3. Provide clean, documented commands for cloning, installing, creating data, training, evaluating, and interpreting results.
4. Simplify/replace the old Python-code-generation experiment implementation if this yields a smaller and clearer repository. It is **acceptable to delete obsolete application/training/benchmark files**, but do not indiscriminately wipe the repository, rewrite history, or remove collaboration policies.

The immediate goal is to observe a clear improvement **on this well-specified synthetic task** and verify the training/evaluation workflow. It is *not* to prove general coding ability or real-world freight extraction competence.

## Context

- Target repository: `takahirox/llm-finetuning`, default branch `main`.
- Reference upstream: https://github.com/openatlaspro-AI/mlx-lora-finetune at commit `24f663d1a276203356d957d6e340ee2182ff83d8` (pin this reference for reproducibility; inspect exact source, recipes, dataset-generation rules, results and MIT licensing before reuse).
- Upstream recipe reported in README: `mlx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit`, 8 LoRA layers, rank 8, 600 optimizer iterations, batch size 4, learning rate `1e-4`, 150 synthetic held-out tests. Reported training duration ~6m14s on a particular Apple Silicon Mac is **not** a runtime guarantee.
- Existing repository has Apple Silicon/MLX dependencies and Qwen3-4B MBPP/HumanEval/data-quality pipelines. The latter may be removed or clearly archived as legacy if not needed for this new focused goal.
- Issue #11 / PR #12 may still be open while #13 / PR #14 has merged. **Inspect the current branch, PRs and collaborator-facing files during implementation; do not silently delete or overwrite work associated with an open PR.** Document any intentional scope change/conflict and keep the decision visible.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/AGENTS.md), the [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md); new Issue/PR/docs and commit messages must be English.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Faithful reproduction
- [ ] Inspect and pin the upstream reference commit, model identifier (and immutable revision if available), data-generation algorithm/seed/splits, scoring rules, prompt/chat template, schema and normalization, and LoRA settings. Record any divergence from the reference as an explicit intentional difference. Verify source licensing/attribution.
- [ ] Add a simple Apple Silicon setup using pinned or reproducibly locked dependencies. Prioritize an upstream-faithful positive-control workflow over preserving unrelated old abstractions. Document the minimum supported machine/software conditions and a quick environment check.
- [ ] Deterministically generate or verify the upstream-style **train/validation/test split**; assert sizes and no duplicate/leaked IDs or examples across splits. Keep the 150-example held-out test set excluded from training, selection and prompt examples.
- [ ] Train a **new** LoRA adapter locally from the 4-bit 0.5B checkpoint (do not report upstream's committed adapter or stored results as a new run). Record the recipe, model and data fingerprints, seed, timestamps and version information. Store model caches and generated adapter weights outside Git; never commit large artifacts or credentials.
- [ ] Evaluate base vs new LoRA on the **same** held-out records, with identical prompts, decoding/scoring settings, field normalization and software environment. Report JSON-valid fraction, exact-record accuracy and each field's exact-match fraction (origin, destination, weight_lbs, mode, on_time), with numerators/denominators, before/after deltas and basic per-example outcomes.
- [ ] Compare freshly measured metrics with the upstream reported **71.3% → 100.0%** reference, *without making exact matching results a prerequisite*. If results differ, investigate data, prompt, model, version, training and scoring differences and report findings honestly. Do not alter the test data/scorer after viewing results merely to reach the upstream score.

### Repository simplification and documentation
- [ ] Remove/replace superseded MBPP/HumanEval/Qwen3 pipeline source, configs, tests and obsolete docs **only after inspecting their dependencies and any outstanding PRs**. Preserve useful Git history (normal commits, no force push), `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`, PR template, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/development-flow.md`, `docs/review-guidelines.md`, and all necessary navigation links. Update README so it truthfully describes the new project. State clearly what legacy components were retired and why.
- [ ] Do not delete local ignored data, models, checkpoints or historical results on a developer's machine; do not mutate prior experiment artifacts. Keep generated data/results/weights ignored unless tiny reproducible fixtures or suitable non-sensitive summary results are justified.
- [ ] Add focused automated tests for deterministic generation/split integrity, schema and canonicalization, prompt consistency, scoring and result aggregation, and saved-result compatibility. Run relevant static/unit checks and document outcomes.
- [ ] Provide **copy-and-run commands** for data preparation, fresh training, base/adapted scoring, and comparison, plus a clear short final report with actual executed steps, metrics, limitations and any checks not performed.
- [ ] Submit an Issue-linked PR to `main`; follow the repository's normal review/merge guidance. Keep the implementation focused on this single baseline replication rather than adding additional model/data sweeps.

## Optional validation

- On Apple Silicon with suitable memory, reproduce the full upstream experiment including real model download, fresh LoRA training and paired 150-example scoring prior to merge, and record runtime/memory if measured. If the implementation environment lacks hardware, implement and validate what is possible and explicitly **do not claim the reported improvement was reproduced**; provide the precise local command sequence for later execution.
- Evaluate a separately generated synthetic variation after the fixed upstream reproduction (without tuning to it) to probe transfer. This is optional and must not replace the faithful primary comparison.

## Required post-merge verification

None automatically required. A merge does not itself run training or the benchmark. Distinguish any remaining real-device experiment from already completed pre-merge checks.
